svg.title: Rejection comparison on aligned recurrent steps
svg.desc: Both panels start at x0 and use the same recurrent-step columns. Block verification occupies three steps in one forward. Drop and restart are shown for both paths.
svg.text: Same start, same mismatch: accept x1, reject x2, produce corrected x2′. Target = 4 loops; draft = 1 loop; block K = 4.
S1–S8 align RECURRENT loop executions, not measured time. P / C and GPU-ready results are shown; their durations are not represented.
P = PRELUDE · C = CODA. Processing xi predicts the NEXT token. Red means computed and then discarded; prime denotes the corrected branch.
S1–S5: shallow steps. S6–S8: one verification forward through R2–R4. DROP after S8; restart at S9.
At S8 discard old x2–x4 and their invalid predictions. The next block would restart from x2′ after the displayed S8 boundary.
S1–S3: fill. S4: produce x1. S5: correct x2 and DROP. S6: restart from x2′. S6–S8: refill the corrected branch.
Both panels end at S8. Pipeline S6–S8 refill from x2′; no further target result is ready within this window.
Column alignment explains the execution sequence only. More or fewer steps alone do not establish a measured latency or throughput gain.
Only valid tokens and used P/C results are shown; inactive/padding rows and unused computations are omitted.
Async: copy-stream D2H and CPU collect occur later; GPU progress does not wait for CPU delivery.
